questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Which of the following best distinguishes Reinforcement Learning (RL) from Supervised Learning? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[RL uses delayed rewards while Supervised Learning uses immediate and labeled feedback.]]>
<![CDATA[RL uses labeled data while Supervised Learning does not.]]>
<![CDATA[Supervised Learning optimizes cumulative rewards.]]>
<![CDATA[RL cannot operate in dynamic environments.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[In reinforcement learning, what is the primary role of the agent? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[To define the environment]]>
<![CDATA[To maximize cumulative rewards through interactions]]>
<![CDATA[To provide feedback to the environment]]>
<![CDATA[To observe only the current reward]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[What is the main purpose of the Bellman Equation in reinforcement learning? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[To calculate gradients for neural networks]]>
<![CDATA[To determine policy randomness]]>
<![CDATA[To recursively estimate the value of states or state-action pairs]]>
<![CDATA[To initialize Q-values arbitrarily]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Why is balancing exploration and exploitation important in RL? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[Because exploration reduces the model accuracy]]>
<![CDATA[To avoid infinite loops during training]]>
<![CDATA[To ensure the agent gathers information while maximizing rewards]]>
<![CDATA[Because exploitation avoids computational cost]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Which of the following is a limitation of Monte Carlo methods in RL? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[They cannot estimate value functions.]]>
<![CDATA[They require knowledge of model dynamics.]]>
<![CDATA[They are not suitable for continuous or non-episodic tasks.]]>
<![CDATA[They rely on the Bellman equation for updates.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[What is the key difference between Monte Carlo (MC) and Temporal Difference (TD) methods? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[MC methods update values incrementally, while TD waits till end of episode.]]>
<![CDATA[MC methods require a model, TD does not.]]>
<![CDATA[TD methods use full return, MC uses estimated rewards.]]>
<![CDATA[MC methods require the Bellman optimality equation.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[What distinguishes the SARSA algorithm from Q-Learning? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[SARSA is an off-policy algorithm while Q-Learning is on-policy.]]>
<![CDATA[Q-Learning updates the policy with exploration, SARSA does not.]]>
<![CDATA[SARSA updates using the next action from the same policy; Q-Learning uses greedy action for update.]]>
<![CDATA[Q-Learning does not use a reward function.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Which of the following is a key benefit of Temporal Difference (TD) learning? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[It requires full knowledge of the environment's transition probabilities.]]>
<![CDATA[It only works in episodic environments.]]>
<![CDATA[It combines advantages of both DP and Monte Carlo methods.]]>
<![CDATA[It avoids bootstrapping.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[In the epsilon-greedy strategy, what does epsilon represent? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[The probability of choosing the greedy action]]>
<![CDATA[The probability of choosing a random action]]>
<![CDATA[The value of the best reward so far]]>
<![CDATA[The discount factor]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Why is Thompson Sampling considered effective in solving MAB problems? (variant 1)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[It avoids exploration entirely]]>
<![CDATA[It deterministically selects the best arm]]>
<![CDATA[It uses a Bayesian approach to balance exploration and exploitation]]>
<![CDATA[It requires prior knowledge of all arm distributions]]>

<![CDATA[To avoid infinite loops during training]]>
<![CDATA[To ensure the agent gathers information while maximizing rewards]]>
<![CDATA[Because exploitation avoids computational cost]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Which of the following is a limitation of Monte Carlo methods in RL? (variant 9)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[They cannot estimate value functions.]]>
<![CDATA[They require knowledge of model dynamics.]]>
<![CDATA[They are not suitable for continuous or non-episodic tasks.]]>
<![CDATA[They rely on the Bellman equation for updates.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[What is the key difference between Monte Carlo (MC) and Temporal Difference (TD) methods? (variant 9)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[MC methods update values incrementally, while TD waits till end of episode.]]>
<![CDATA[MC methods require a model, TD does not.]]>
<![CDATA[TD methods use full return, MC uses estimated rewards.]]>
<![CDATA[MC methods require the Bellman optimality equation.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[What distinguishes the SARSA algorithm from Q-Learning? (variant 9)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[SARSA is an off-policy algorithm while Q-Learning is on-policy.]]>
<![CDATA[Q-Learning updates the policy with exploration, SARSA does not.]]>
<![CDATA[SARSA updates using the next action from the same policy; Q-Learning uses greedy action for update.]]>
<![CDATA[Q-Learning does not use a reward function.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Which of the following is a key benefit of Temporal Difference (TD) learning? (variant 9)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[It requires full knowledge of the environment's transition probabilities.]]>
<![CDATA[It only works in episodic environments.]]>
<![CDATA[It combines advantages of both DP and Monte Carlo methods.]]>
<![CDATA[It avoids bootstrapping.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[In the epsilon-greedy strategy, what does epsilon represent? (variant 9)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[The probability of choosing the greedy action]]>
<![CDATA[The probability of choosing a random action]]>
<![CDATA[The value of the best reward so far]]>
<![CDATA[The discount factor]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Why is Thompson Sampling considered effective in solving MAB problems? (variant 9)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[It avoids exploration entirely]]>
<![CDATA[It deterministically selects the best arm]]>
<![CDATA[It uses a Bayesian approach to balance exploration and exploitation]]>
<![CDATA[It requires prior knowledge of all arm distributions]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[Which of the following best distinguishes Reinforcement Learning (RL) from Supervised Learning? (variant 10)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[RL uses delayed rewards while Supervised Learning uses immediate and labeled feedback.]]>
<![CDATA[RL uses labeled data while Supervised Learning does not.]]>
<![CDATA[Supervised Learning optimizes cumulative rewards.]]>
<![CDATA[RL cannot operate in dynamic environments.]]>

questiontext.text: <![CDATA[In reinforcement learning, what is the primary role of the agent? (variant 10)]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[To define the environment]]>
<![CDATA[To maximize cumulative rewards through interactions]]>
<![CDATA[To provide feedback to the environment]]>
<![CDATA[To observe only the current reward]]>

answer.text: <![CDATA[To calculate gradients for neural networks]]>
<![CDATA[To determine policy randomness]]>
<![CDATA[To recursively estimate the value of states or state-action pairs]]>
<![CDATA[To initialize Q-values arbitrarily]]>
